curation.notes: In vitro single-trap optical tweezers on spherical supported lipid bilayers (SSLBs: 500 nm latex beads, also 3 µm silica, coated with PC or PC:PA 19:1 membranes) carrying endogenous motors recruited from Dictyostelium (dynein) or rat brain (kinesin-1) ATP-releasates; stalls measured against the trap on polarity-marked, surface-adhered microtubules, plus free runs with the trap off, with/without inhibitors KTD-GST and Ciliobrevin-D.

evidence.snippet: QPD data was digitized at 2 kHz for recording SSLB motion. To calibrate the trap, thermal fluctuations of SSLBs were recorded at 40 kHz and the corner frequency was determined.
Trap stiffness was adjusted between 0.05 pN/nm to 0.15 pN/nm, depending on the experiment.

bead_size.note: latex SSLB core; larger 3 µm silica SSLBs also used for size dependence

evidence.snippet: These liposomes were then deposited onto a latex bead of 500nm diameter, as described in Figure 1A (also see STAR Methods).

evidence.snippet: Phosphatidylcholine (PC; for PC liposomes) or PC and Phosphatidic acid (PA) in the molar ratio 19:1 (for PA liposomes) were dried in a nitrogen stream to form lipid films.
SSLBs containing phosphatidic acid recruit dynein when incubated with Dictyostelium fractions but kinesin-1 when incubated with rat brain fractions.
